items.quote:
local function Table(parent, key)
	if type(parent[key]) ~= "table" then
		parent[key] = {}
	end
	return parent[key]
end
items.what: Table(parent, key) generalizes a single vendor-table initialization in InitPrices; both parameters are fixed and its return value is discarded.
items.why: Whole-repository searches for Table and InitPrices across Lua, XML, TOC, Python, shell, workflows, docs and types found only the local definition and Table(ns.db, "vendor") in Prices.lua. The function is neither exported nor registered, and no second use or implementation exists in the tree. Replace the call with the same three-line type guard on ns.db.vendor inside InitPrices and remove the generic helper. This preserves initialization and existing persisted vendor data while removing two unnecessary parameters and an unused return; it does not remove the guard or change the saved schema.
items.guard: lens-only: spotting a single-caller helper whose arguments are always the same needs whole-file judgment

items.what: InitPrices re-validates ns.db.vendor, which LoadDB has already guaranteed is a table
items.why: Core.lua:407-408 runs LoadDB (its DEFAULTS loop at Core.lua:83-87 resets any non-table vendor to {}) immediately before InitPrices, and it is the only caller outside specs; prices_spec.lua:13 and model_spec always supply vendor = {}. The guard cannot fire.
items.reason: The guard supports model_spec's real partial-load initialization, where db.vendor has not been created by Core.LoadDB; removing it in memory causes Price to index nil at Prices.lua:98. The defensive-noise partial-load exception applies despite the full TOC path having validated the DB.

items.quote: local each = info.price / math.max(info.stackCount or 1, 1)
items.what: A merchant entry with a missing or zero stackCount is treated as a one-item stack, and the guessed unit price is persisted as an observed vendor price.
items.why: RecordMerchant checks that price is positive but never establishes the stack size. The pinned MerchantItemInfo declaration in .types/vscode-wow-api/Annotations/Core/Blizzard_APIDocumentationGenerated/MerchantFrameDocumentation.lua marks stackCount optional with default 0. An in-memory LuaJIT MERCHANT_SHOW repro using an item ID and price=100 recorded ns.db.vendor[itemID]=100 and returned Price(itemID).copper=100 with either absent stackCount or stackCount=0. That record takes precedence over ns.VendorPrices in Price and survives subsequent sessions, so unknown quantity becomes authoritative price data. Skip recording until a positive stack size is known, preserving any previously known unit price.
items.reason: owner-delegated 2026-09-27: merchant rows need a positive stackCount
items.guard: lens-only: prices_spec covers zero and missing stack sizes; a guessed divisor elsewhere needs judgment

items.quote: if type(ns.db.vendor) ~= "table" then
items.what: unreachable branch: InitPrices re-defaults ns.db.vendor
items.why: Core.lua LoadDB runs immediately before ns.InitPrices (only caller) and its DEFAULTS loop already resets any non-table vendor to {}; prices_spec loads Prices.lua directly but sets its own ns.db. Not persisted-data compat (LoadDB covers it). Low value; deletion needs the spec to supply db.vendor.
items.reason: The branch is reachable in a supported partial load, not dead: model_spec constructs db with craftValue but no vendor and then calls InitPrices before Price. Removing this initializer in memory fails at Prices.lua:98 from model_spec:379; same producer as 97c985eec0.

items.quote: return copper, okAge and type(days) == "number" and days or nil
items.what: A failed or missing GetAuctionAgeByItemID call gives days = nil, the same value as 'seen more than three weeks ago'
items.why: AuctionatorAPI() only checks GetAuctionPriceByItemID, so a build without the age function makes pcall fail. Tooltip.lua PriceAgeText then says 'over 3 weeks ago' and PriceAge counts 22 days, so Route.lua PriceAge shows every route in orange with 'rescan with Auctionator'. Unknown age should render as unknown, not as an invented 22 days.
items.reason: With a valid auction price but missing GetAuctionAgeByItemID, the unchanged price path returns days=nil; Tooltip.PriceAgeText then says over 3 weeks ago and PriceAge returns 1,900,800 seconds. The probe distinguishes missing capability from Auctionator's intentional old-age nil sentinel, so unknown age is incorrectly presented as known stale data.

items.quote:
while rank and segment.toSkill - profession.modifier > rank.cap - 75 do
			steps[#steps + 1] = { rank = rank }
items.what: Bug: a segment crossing a skill cap can place rank training before the player meets its required skill.
items.why:
RouteSteps tests the segment endpoint and inserts the rank before the whole segment, without checking its starting skill against rank.reqSkill or splitting the segment. With bundled Heavy Linen Bandage thresholds, First Aid 40/75 targeting 90 produces 'Train Journeyman at 50' followed by one craft segment from 40 to 90. The first action is impossible at 40. RenderRoute and API.lua Steps consume this order directly; RequiresLine also assumes the route has reached the prerequisite before training. The ordered route needs a craft segment reaching the training point before this rank, followed by the remaining crafts. Executed an in-memory LuaJIT reproduction from the repository root (no files written):
luajit - <<'LUA'
local ns = {db={trainer={},routeTargets={}}, InvalidateAPI=function() end}
local known, costs = {}, {}
ns.IsLearned=function(id) return known[id] == true end
ns.NetCost=function(id) return costs[id] end
local env=setmetatable({APPRENTICE='Apprentice', JOURNEYMAN='Journeyman', EXPERT='Expert', ARTISAN='Artisan'}, {__index=_G})
for _,file in ipairs({'Locales/enUS.lua','Data/Thresholds.lua','Data/Recipes.lua','Data/Trainer.lua','Model.lua','Route.lua'}) do
  setfenv(assert(loadfile(file)),env)('SkillUpForever',ns)
end
known[3275], costs[3275], known[3276], costs[3276] = true, 1, true, 1
ns.db.routeTargets[129]=90
local p={skillLine=129,name='First Aid',skill=40,base=40,max=75,modifier=0,capped=false}
local r=ns.PlanRoute(p)
local s=ns.RouteSteps(p,r)
assert(s[1].rank.reqSkill==50 and s[1].rank.reqSkill>p.base)
assert(s[2].segment.recipeID==3276 and s[2].segment.fromSkill==40 and s[2].segment.toSkill==90)
print(s[1].rank.name,s[1].rank.reqSkill,s[2].segment.fromSkill,s[2].segment.toSkill) -- Journeyman 50 40 90
LUA
items.reason: Fixed at the producer: ns.PlanRoute now splits a segment that crosses a rank's cap from below its reqSkill (SplitAtRank), so these RouteSteps lines, still correct, place the rank between the halves (route_spec 'crafts up to the skill Journeyman needs'). The quote stays, so the ledger cannot record fixed; re-anchor on the next audit

		-- Auctionator knows only what it has scanned, so installing it isn't enough.
items.what: Bug: an unpriced, already-grey recipe hides valid continuation suggestions and gives an irrelevant pricing explanation.

RenderRoute treats any positive count as proof that prices caused the blockage; its elseif then prevents RenderSuggestions. A real-data repro at Tailoring 100/150, target 125, with known unpriced recipe 2393 has six eligible scroll suggestions from Sources.lua, but RenderRoute never asks for them and shows only the Auctionator message. Pricing that grey recipe cannot let it skill up. Filter pricing blockers to recipes that could still help, and allow no_recipe suggestions even when pricing information is also shown. The repro obtains private render functions through debug.getupvalue in the headless LuaJIT harness; it does not create or operate client frames. Executed an in-memory LuaJIT reproduction from the repository root (no files written):

env.tContains=function(t,v) for _,x in ipairs(t) do if x==v then return true end end return false end

ns.HasAuctionator=function() return false end
known[2393]=true
ns.db.routeTargets[197]=125
local p={skillLine=197,name='Tailoring',skill=100,base=100,max=150,modifier=0,capped=false}
local r=ns.PlanRoute(p)
assert(#r.segments==0 and r.excluded.unpriced==1 and ns.Model.Color(ns.Model.Get(2393),p.skill)=='grey')

items.quote: if price and price.source == "auctionator" and (not oldest or ns.PriceAge(price) > ns.PriceAge(oldest)) then
items.what: PriceAge re-fetches ns.Price for each reagent and re-decides 'is this an auction price' by the literal "auctionator", although each SkillUpNeededItem already carries the bucketed source ("auction"). Two vocabularies for one concept: price sources 'vendor'|'auctionator'|'gather' (compared by literal in Tooltip.lua:125/134/160, Model.lua:250, Route.lua:535/631, API.lua:114/133) and reagent buckets 'gather'|'vendor'|'auction'|'unknown'; the "auctionator means auction" mapping is restated here and in Model.ShoppingList.
items.why: Profile Anti-patterns names exactly this shape. SkillUpPriceSource is an alias (types/Namespace.lua:234) but LuaLS does not check equality comparisons against it, so a typo or a new source (e.g. a second AH addon) silently yields no price-age line. The guard is needed only because ns.PriceAge (Tooltip.lua:124) errors on non-auctionator prices; filtering on item.source == "auction" would read the already-computed bucket instead of restating the mapping.
items.reason: Price provenance (SkillUpPriceSource literal union) and acquisition buckets are distinct typed contracts; PriceAge reads Auctionator-specific age metadata, so 'auctionator' there is not the bucket

if target > rank.cap - 75 then
			route.ranks[#route.ranks + 1] = rank
			route.trainingCost = route.trainingCost + rank.fee
items.what: Bug: incomplete plans charge rank-training fees for skill caps the route never reaches.
items.why:

items.quote: local stack = math.max(info.stackCount or 1, 1)
items.what: A missing or nonpositive merchant stackCount is silently replaced with one, inventing the unit basis for the displayed cost and automatic purchase quantities.
items.why: MerchantPurchases accepts an item record with a positive price without validating its stackCount, then uses the substituted one to round purchase units and divide the stack price. RefreshBuyButton displays that cost and BuyMissing uses those quantities and the cost for its affordability check. Repository-wide searches found the same fallback in Prices.lua but no documented contract making one the correct substitute for unavailable stack data. An in-memory LuaJIT reproduction invoked the unchanged MerchantPurchases with seven missing units and a price of 100: nil, zero and negative stackCount each yielded stack=1, count=7 and cost=700; a stackCount of five yielded count=10 and cost=200. The invalid inputs were synthetic, so this demonstrates the fallback and its downstream effect, not that the client currently emits these records. Under the project convention, unknown quantity data should remain unknown rather than become a plausible purchase.
items.reason: The pinned MerchantItemInfo contract allows missing stackCount and defaults it to 0 without guaranteeing a positive price implies a positive quantity; Shopping substitutes one, unlike Prices' validated merchant observer. The unchanged-path probe calculates count=7/cost=700 for nil, zero or negative stack versus count=10/cost=200 for stack=5, proving invented purchase and affordability quantities for allowed incomplete data.

	if skill < t[1] then

	end

items.quote: nativeAnchor.y + shift
items.what: Layout places the host at the saved native anchor four times with the same five-field SetPoint(nativeAnchor.point, relativeTo, relativePoint, x, y): lines 201-207 (combat), 227-233, 256-262 and 274-280 (last adds `+ shift`). Same for the repeated `host.GetEffectiveScale and host:GetEffectiveScale() or 1` / UIParent scale pair at 191, 234-235, 265-266.
items.why: One local helper (e.g. PlaceHost(yOffset)) and one scale-ratio helper would be the single home; the copies are identical apart from the y offset, so an anchor rule change (e.g. a new field) must be made in every one.
items.reason: Combat uses StackPoints' bottom edge rather than nativeAnchor.point; the other anchors occur before content layout, after height is known and after off-screen correction adds shift, so they observe different geometry epochs. These short SetPoint API idioms do not constitute duplicated policy, and the scale guards are covered by Settled Client-capability checks.

items.quote: seen[service.recipeID] = { GetTrainerServiceCost(index), required or 0 }
items.what: A missing required skill from GetTrainerServiceSkillReq is saved as 0 into SkillUpForeverDB.trainer, and ns.TrainingFor (Route.lua:96-99) then prefers this saved entry over the bundled ns.TrainerFees value, so a real requirement is replaced by an invented 'no requirement'.
items.why: Route.lua:113 computes taught[1] = max(t[1], training[2] + modifier); with 0 the route may plan the recipe from its orange threshold even when the trainer requires more (the reason the saved value exists, per the comment at Trainer.lua:95-96). Store nil (or skip the entry / keep the bundled value) when the client gives no requirement. Low: max() with t[1] masks it whenever the orange threshold equals the requirement, which is the common case.
items.reason: Superseded, not refuted: the quoted code now lives at Integrations/Trainer.lua and the item is carried as c31e2bf759, which holds the verdict.

items.quote: text = string.format("%s  |cff808080%s|r", RecipeName(suggestion.recipeID), suggestion.kindText),
items.what: Hand-written colour escape `|cff808080...|r` (also Route.lua:337, UI/Shopping.lua:315 and :340, UI/Tooltip.lua:185 and :208) where the client's ColorMixin does it: GRAY_FONT_COLOR:WrapTextInColorCode(text). The same file already uses GRAY_FONT_COLOR (326, 423, 431) and WrapTextInColorCode (84, 85).
items.why: GRAY_FONT_COLOR is 0.5, 0.5, 0.5, the same ff808080, so output is unchanged; check the rendered hex matches in the Forever client before replacing. The magic hex is repeated six times across three files.
items.reason: Nothing is hand-rolled: `|cff808080...|r` is the client's own colour markup written as a literal, and ColorMixin:WrapTextInColorCode is only another way to build the same string, with no behaviour the literal lacks. The project writes literal escapes for its other one-off colours (UI/Tooltip.lua:115, Core/Core.lua:68 and :399), four of the six sites sit inside a string.format pattern (UI/Tooltip.lua:185, :208, UI/Route.lua:233, :337), and the finding itself says the Forever client's hex must be checked, while tests/shopping_spec.lua:55 pins the literal.

items.quote: -- A day-old Auctionator price is flagged: auction prices move that fast.
items.what: stale: the comment says a day-old price is flagged
items.why: Carried from ledger item 13ad7d49a8, recorded against the file before it moved to UI/Route.lua. Auctionator reports whole days and PriceAge is days * 86400 (Tooltip.lua:128). The test is `ns.PriceAge(oldest) > STALE_AFTER` with STALE_AFTER = 86400, so days = 1 gives 86400 > 86400 = false and is not flagged. Flagging starts at 2 days, or when the age is unknown (22 days). Either the comment should say 'older than a day' (as 2+ days) or the comparison should be >=.
items.guard: lens-only: a comment's threshold against the comparison below it needs a reader
